population.span: Children (aged 3 months to 14 years) with common infections were enrolled in a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial

endpoint.span: AAD (diarrhoea caused by Clostridium difficile or otherwise unexplained diarrhoea)

estimate.span: Three (2.5%) children in the probiotic group developed AAD (diarrhoea caused by Clostridium difficile or otherwise unexplained diarrhoea) compared to nine (7.5%) in the placebo group (RR 0.33, 95% CI 0.1-1.06).

ci.span: Three (2.5%) children in the probiotic group developed AAD (diarrhoea caused by Clostridium difficile or otherwise unexplained diarrhoea) compared to nine (7.5%) in the placebo group (RR 0.33, 95% CI 0.1-1.06).

analysis_set.span: Analyses were by intention to treat.

treatment_strategy.span: they received standard antibiotic treatment plus 2 x 10(10) colony forming units of a probiotic (n = 120) or a placebo (n = 120), administered orally twice daily throughout antibiotic treatment.

absent_reason.follow_up: Both abstracts explicitly give the window during or up to 2 weeks after antibiotic therapy for any diarrhoea, but do not explicitly state the timepoint for the separately reported AAD estimate.

entry_population_matches_question.why: The randomized children received antibiotics, matching the question's population; analyses were explicitly intention to treat.
